# Hirelings of the Old World

*Pages PDF 3-24*

## Hirelings of the Old World • Introduction
The Old World is a place shaped by legends. In taverns and homes, huddled by the hearth, people tell tales of mighty heroes whose deeds echo through the ages. Yet the world is not made of such people. Behind every great warrior or wizard there stands countless underlings getting the actual work done. From the insalubrious Streng, companion to Witch Hunter Matthias Thulman, to faithful Chlod, manservant of Bretonnia, these figures may be hidden, but without them who would carry the hero’s bags? 

**Hirelings of the Old World** presents four NPCs for GMs to bring into their games, ready to help the Characters in their adventures, or serve their enemies should they get a better offer. These expand upon the rules for Hirelings (WFRP, page 309) and can help GMs show that they are not simple trappings, but people with their own stories, desires, and perhaps even obstacles for the players to overcome. 

Each NPC comes with a full background, statistics for use in play, and an employer they’re currently serving. They also feature specific requirements needed to hire them, as well as Adventure Hooks to help build their relationship with the Characters. These culminate in a Prestige Adventure, potentially serving as the basis for a whole campaign. 

## **How Shall I Use This?**
There are many ways to use this PDF. It can provide NPCs to interact with the Characters; Hirelings to assist with their adventures or grant them access to various Endeavours; potential antagonists to add complications to an existing story; or seeds for campaigns in their own right. GMs may wish to use the rules for Favours (WFRP, page 198) both as a reward for completing an NPC’s tasks and as incentive to take them on. 

## **Endeavours for Hire**
Each NPC can help with, or even carry out, specific Endeavours on the Characters’ behalf, for a price. Their services can be engaged both during the Between Adventures phase, or while the Characters are otherwise occupied with an adventure. The party can take care of business while, for example, Liriwen Amberbloom gathers information on a mark for them. As Hirelings make their living by their talents, you will always be able to hire them for this purpose, unless they are otherwise engaged, but gaining their trust may reduce the costs required. Some NPCs do not value coin as highly as others, preferring to trade goods or services in kind. 

## **Employee of the Month**
Hirelings go where the job is, and aren’t generally found at a fixed abode. Instead, they might turn up in the service of specific employers and can therefore be encountered wherever the story needs them. Each NPC has an entry detailing an employer for whom they might work. Alternatively, they could be in the service of an existing NPC within your campaign, perhaps even a longstanding antagonist looking for more information about the Hireling’s former associates or serving as a spy in the Characters’ ranks. They could also turn up working for the NPCs from Patrons of the Old World I and II, allowing a GM to bring a new spin to an adventure as their different aims come into competition, the Characters stuck in the middle. 

## **Luhrguhr ‘Lantern’ Angryfist**
## **Ogre Mercenary**
## **Motivation:** Revenge
**Short-term Ambition:** Survive the agents of the Stirland aristocracy. 

**Long-term Ambition:** Devour the horn-crowned Beastman’s gut. 

While travelling the trading outposts, fishing villages, and smugglers dens littering the Old World’s rivers, you might spy an Ogre sporting an impressive collection of Stirland military medals. It would be unwise to stare too long though, for while he is an affable soul, this Ogre carries a spark of paranoia always waiting to flare into violence. 

Born into the Angryfist tribe high in the mountains, Lantern grew up hearing stories about the Empire from the tribe’s (often terrified) Human Firemaster. These tales sparked the young Ogre’s wanderlust and he set out in search of these lands filled with plunder for any who’ll fight for it. 

**LUHRGUHR ANGRYFIST OGRE DOCKHAND, FORMER GUARD (BRASS 3)**

Lantern took employment in the Stirland military, who found feeding the brute a meagre fee when compared to having someone who could both guard their cannons and carry them off the battlefield afterwards. It was here he was given the nickname ‘Lantern,’ ostensibly for his prominent jawline, though the uncharitable say it’s because he’s not that bright. It also marked the beginning of an unlikely friendship, as Lantern came to the attention of the army’s young commander. 

This general, a distant relation of Graf Alberich HauptAnderson, was still fresh from his home’s sheltered confines. Now, with a chance to prove himself, he found himself stymied by overbearing advisers who thought they knew better just because they had led armies before. 

After seeing Lantern drive off an Ungor ambush by hurling cannonballs at them, he thought he spied a solution to his problem. He promoted the Ogre to his personal bodyguard and was amazed at how eagerly his subordinates accepted orders if it meant getting away from Lantern’s glare. Lantern, for his part, revelled in the fine food and prestige his new position brought, and the two became inseparable. 

It was not to last. As the army marched one day, a Beastman warherd erupted from the treeline. Lantern waded into the rampaging Gors, his great war club rising and falling in 

bloody arcs. They fell back from him and Lantern gave chase. It wasn’t until the Gors melted into the forest’s shadows that he turned to find his friend lying dead on the ground. 

He caught only a glimpse of his killer: a colossal Beastman, marked by a crown of horns sprouting from his skull. 

Saddened by his friend’s passing, Lantern ate his body as a gesture of respect, gifting him to the Great Maw. The soldiers standing nearby did not quite see this in the same light. 

Cast out, Lantern began chasing the horn-crowned Beastman throughout the Old World, eager to take his revenge. His search was complicated by the general’s family placing a bounty on Lantern’s head, seeking retribution for the desecration of their scion’s corpse. Lantern realised that, sooner or later, there would be too many bounty hunters to fight. He resolved to keep his head down, and took a job in a smuggling crew, hiding amidst the Empire’s many waterways (while never taking his medals off — he has his pride). Now, he travels aboard _The Gull Maraz_ , keeping a suspicious eye out for anyone seeking Stirland coin, and always searching for the horncrowned Beastman. 

## **Captain Frisal and** _the Gull Maraz_
Captain Frisal and the crew of _The Gull Maraz_ make their living shipping grain up and down the Teufel. At least, that’s what it says on the paperwork. Frisal is a smuggler, however, and is willing to stuff their hold’s hidden compartments with anything that might fetch a price. Luxuries, heretical texts, Elven artefacts; all these and more have slipped past the river warden’s watchful gaze. 

The captain was more than happy to bring Lantern onboard. The Ogre doesn’t speak much about his past, but that’s not unusual among the river’s less salubrious folk, and a little reticence is a small price for a stevedore who no dock inspector wants to get too close to. 

At first, the crew found Lantern’s easy humour and complete inability to bluff at cards endearing. That was until they got into a bar fight and witnessed him strip a man’s arm to the bone. Now, most keep their distance, whispering dark rumours about the Ogre’s appetites. 

Even Frisal is starting to have doubts. Every now and then, people with Stirland accents and an anxious air turn up asking questions, and they never seem to be able to dock for long without Lantern getting into some sort of trouble. They tried asking him about his past once. The way his lip peeled back to reveal sharp, shark-like teeth made them re-think this approach. For the time being, the Ogre is an asset, but if word of the bounty on his head ever reached the captain… well, then it might be time to consider just how valuable he may truly be. 

## **The Gull Maraz**
_The Gull Maraz_ appears to be a regular river barge. However, Captain Frisal has spent a great deal ensuring it can outrun any patrol boat, should they get too nosey. It keeps a crew of eight, including Lantern and Frisal. 

You can find expanded rules for boats in Death on the Reik Companion. _The Gull Maraz_ counts as a Typical Barge (DRC, page 33) improved with Hull Smoothing (DRC, page 64), a Stripped Superstructure (DRC, page 66), and a Racing Rig (DRC, page 66). 

## **Lantern’s Menu Gaolhouse Rock**
Captain Frisal’s prized dockhand has gone missing and they need that blasted Ogre to get The Gull Maraz loaded up before rainwaters hit. In desperation, they’re willing to offer free passage to anyone who can find Lantern. However, Lantern is sleeping off a hangover in chains. A local Watch patrol found him passed out next to a barrel of ale, surrounded by bloody pieces. Now they’re waiting for word from higher up on what to do and praying to Sigmar the Ogre doesn’t wake up first. 

## **A Midnight Snack**
The crew left Lantern to protect the boat while they went ashore to get some proper drinking done. Unfortunately, Lantern got rather hungry during the night, and one of the items they were smuggling smelled so very tasty… Now, he’s in danger of losing his place on the crew if the captain finds out. He needs the Characters to find a replacement. He’s not sure what it was, but it tasted great. Asked who it was intended for he says ‘I dunno slim, but far as I can work it out it was some bony wizardy type.’ Bony in this case may mean an Amethyst Wizard, Necromancer, or someone who is slender compared to an Ogre. 

## **You Do the Talkin’**
Beastmen raided a nearby village, so Lantern is planning to pay the place a visit. However, he has learned from experience that folks after a Beastman attack aren’t too keen about an Ogre turning up, so he needs the Characters to come do the talking. Arriving at the village, the Characters are greeted by burnt out houses, destitute peasants, mutated trees, and a tavern that appears mysteriously untouched. 

## **Stirring Up Stirland**
While docked for a few days, Lantern spotted a procession of people dressed in Stirland livery. One of them even talked to Captain Frisal, though he doesn’t know what about. What are they doing there, eh? They must be following him. They’re always following him. Well, Lantern will take care of them first. He just needs the Characters to keep his crew distracted, while he goes to that big, old mansion he saw them heading to. 

## **For Hire: Muscle in**
Lantern can be hired by anyone, unless they are wearing Stirland livery in which case he tries to avoid them. He may accompany characters on adventures, carry an extra 15 Encumbrance points, or smash anything that needs smashing. 

Characters can also send Lantern out to Intimidate someone, or deliver a package, but if he is unaccompanied there is always the risk the Ogre might take things too far. If Lantern fails a **Challenging (+0) Willpower** Test, he decides that carnivorous violence is the best way forward. Lantern costs 6/– for a Quick Job, 1 GC Daily, and 6 GC Weekly. He will accept his wages in coin or in the equivalent cost in meat. 

## **Prestige Adventure: a Gut Feeling**
_The horn-crowned Beastman has been sighted. While drinking in a local tavern, Lantern overheard a group of pedlars huddled around the fire, exchanging whispered stories about Beastmen in the forests nearby. More and more of the mutated things are gathering, they say, led by a brutal champion blessed by the Blood God. The monster from Lantern’s past._ 

_After demanding the location from the terrified travellers, Lantern sets off in pursuit. He plans to tear the creature’s gut out and devour it in front of its followers, a well-deserved humiliation for all it has put him through. However, while Lantern may not be the brightest, he learns from his mistakes. He needs the Characters to deal with the thing’s underlings and get him the one-on-one fight he craves._ 

_But it’s not just one warherd they face. Following stories into the forest brings the Characters to a fallen stone circle. They find the horned champion standing ready to face their rival, a Tzeentchian mutant who views their coming as a useful tool in this contest._ 

## **Aftermath**
Should the Characters and Lantern succeed in defeating the horn-crowned Beastman, its warherd scatters, bringing an end to their raids. Producing evidence of the Beastman’s fall earns Lantern his favoured place in the Empire’s armies once more, with commissions offered to the Characters should they agree to hunt down the last of the warherd. 

Lantern does not forget the Characters’ assistance in a hurry, offering to become a Henchman for the party, as per the rules for such characters on WFRP, page 309. 

However, if the Characters do not stop Lantern from eating the Beastman’s gut, he starts to suffer from strange dreams. Crimson dreams. Dreams filled with carnage and bloody vengeance. The Stirland soldiers who cast him aside, the nobles who placed the bounty on his head, the smugglers who cheated and mistrusted him all those years — he sees them all falling to his club. Should this go on too long, the Old World may find itself facing a new champion of the Blood God. 

If the horn-crowned Beastman is not defeated, they continue to build their warherd until at last they have amassed enough power to besiege the human cities. The Characters may be able to use what they have learned about his rivalry with the Tzeentchian mutants to their advantage, but Lantern continues his pursuit. 

## **Liriwen Amberbloom**
## **Wood Elf Spy**
## **Motivation:** Self-Indulgence
**Short-Term Ambition:** Show his superiors his worth. **Long-Term Ambition:** Build his own criminal empire. 

## **Liriwen Amberbloom Wood Elf Spy (Silver 3)**
Among Ubersreik’s criminal underbelly, Liriwen Amberbloom stands out like a flower sprouting from a midden. Dressed in the latest Altdorf fashions, his coat a riot of autumn colours; people are often surprised that this flamboyant figure is becoming one of the underworld’s most highly regarded spies. But, as he often says, when dealing in secrets, people need to find you before they can whisper in your ear. 

A few years ago, Liriwen left his home in the Laurelorn Forest to report on the influence held by Ubersreik’s Dwarf population. The Elf wasn’t there long before he found himself behind bars, a pair of watchmen taking an immediate dislike to him, not helped by a few choice comments he made regarding their mothers. This may have been the best thing that could have happened to him.

While languishing in the squalid gaol, Liriwen was forced to converse with criminals. Far from the ignorant brutes he took them for, he was astonished to find a hitherto untapped source of information, one with roots curling through every layer of Ubersreik’s society. 

When he got out, Liriwen began to ingratiate himself into Ubersreik’s criminal ranks. His skill at slipping through his arboreal realm unnoticed translated well to the city, and he learned their arts of breaking and entering. Soon, they came to accept Liriwen as one of their own and he, to his horror and fascination, found that he rather enjoyed his rowdy, vibrant life among them, so different from the austere home he left behind. 

News travels fast, and people began to seek Liriwen out. Some were simply curious, while others wished to turn the spy to their own aims, wheedling for any hints about the secretive Eonir. Liriwen learned to lean into their curiosity, developing an extravagant persona and spreading tales of his daring break-ins, some of them even true. 

More and more sought him out, providing information and hiring his services, allowing him to fund his revelries and growing appreciation for Ranald’s Delight. 

He found his persona as ‘the Elf in the Red Coat’ a useful ruse. Not only does it draw in business, but it also means he can go unnoticed with a simple clothing change. This has allowed him to infiltrate many city organisations, feeding a steady stream of news back to his superiors in the Laurelorn. 

However, while he has tailored the image he presents in his reports, news of his extravagant ways is beginning to reach those who first sent him. Some are starting to worry their spy has gone native. Liriwen walks a tightrope, needing to prove himself to his superiors without risking the comfortable life he has built. He has no intention of betraying his people. But destiny does not mean for him to moulder away like autumn leaves. 

## **In the Baron’s Employ**
While Liriwen offers his services to all, he is most often found in the employ of The Baron, the ruthless head of the thieves, smugglers, and cutthroats based under the grand Ubersreik bridge. What started as mere curiosity on her part has become a fruitful working relationship. He acts as her eyes and ears, keeping her informed on who is planning what in her city, while she in turn keeps him safe by sheer force of reputation. 

Liriwen finds The Baron a useful patron. Her network extends to places beyond his reach, most notably the Dwarf quarter, Dawihafen. This is something he is keen to cultivate, and he works hard to ensure he always remains in The Baron’s good graces. She is also the surest source of Ranald’s Delight in the city, a substance whose addictive qualities Liriwen is only now beginning to fully grasp. 

He believes he has a good handle on things, for the time being, but hopes The Baron does not realise just how potent a weapon this sword she holds above him has become. 

While The Baron does find Liriwen useful, she cannot deny her personal distaste. The Elf ’s flamboyant nature, coupled with his frequent arrogant comments and unwanted advice on how she should run her enterprises have nearly led to him taking a trip down the Teufel on multiple occasions. One day, perhaps, he will push things too far, and if he ever does anything to threaten all she has built, then the Elf might find the ‘rash and rowdy’ nature of Humans far less endearing than he once thought.

## **Liriwen’s List**
## **Watch My Back**
One of Liriwen’s clients got into a spot of bother with the Watch. Normally, Liriwen would be happy to let the person hang, but he was carrying something he can’t let fall into the hands of either the Watch or The Baron. He needs some people to cause a distraction while he sneaks in to get the evidence, and the Characters look like just the sort to enjoy kicking the hornets’ nest. 

## **Trees Felled at Ground Level**
A Dwarf entrepreneur set up a logging company and is looking for investors, saying she found a hitherto unexploited source of particularly fine lumber. Now, the Old World is full of forests, with no shortage of fools looking to rectify that, but there is something about the Dwarf’s enthusiasm for this venture that has sparked Liriwen’s suspicions. He needs to find out more but is struggling to get closer thanks to her security efforts and strongly held prejudice against Elves. Perhaps the Characters might have better luck. 

## **Sigmarite Slander**
The Baron tasked Liriwen with taking care of a local Witch Hunter who has been sniffing around the Ubersreik Bridge, disrupting her business. However, neither she nor Liriwen are willing to attract the ire of the Sigmarites, so death is out of the question. If something scandalous came to light, that might just prove enough of a distraction, so long as nothing leads back to The Baron or her associates. Shame the Witch Hunter’s reputation is pure as the driven snow. 

## **Sleeping with the Fishes**
A steamship from Barak Varr has arrived, carrying a delegation bearing gifts to the city’s rulers. While the alliance between Humans and Dwarfs has been useful in holding back Chaos, the Eonir are keen to see they don’t get too friendly. Liriwen came up with a plan to plant some incriminating material aboard their boat, for which he needs the Characters’ assistance. Upon boarding, however, they are greeted by the copper tang of blood, and an impossibly lifelike Dwarf statue laid out on a cot. 

**Talents:** Criminal, Embezzle, Etiquette (Criminals), Fearless (Watchmen), Menacing

**Trappings:** Hand Weapon (Cudgel), Mail Coat, Gang of Thieves

## **For Hire: I Spy with My Elf Eye**
Liriwen is prejudiced against watchmen and won’t work with them, unless they prove themselves valuable first. 

Liriwen can be hired to either help with the **Study a Mark** or **The Latest News** Endeavours (WFRP, page 201), or carry them out on the Characters’ behalf. Having him assist changes them from a **Challenging (+0)** to an **Average (+20)** Test but requires the employing Character to accompany him. 

If Liriwen fumbles a Test while in the Characters’ employ, he is spotted with them either by rival criminals or fellow agents from the Laurelorn. They are more likely to act on this the more often they see Liriwen with the Characters. 

## **People of Ubersreik**
Both The Baron and the Harataki clan feature in A Guide to Ubersreik, found in the WFRP Starter Set. Should you wish to expand the Characters’ interactions with them, you can find more information in that supplement. 

## **The Harataki Clan**
Led by Queen Vilda, the Harataki are a well-respected Dwarf clan that made their home in Ubersreik’s Dawihafen after losing their ancestral hold, Karak Branar. They are desperate for any opportunity to reclaim what has been lost and are touchy about their fallen status. Queen Vilda is not one to let an insult pass. 

Liriwen costs 3/– for a Quick Job, 9/– Daily, and 3 GC Weekly. Alternatively, he may accept information useful to him, or Ranald’s Delight in payment. 

## **Prestige Adventures They’ll Rune the Day**
_Liriwen is being called back to the Laurelorn. It appears his superiors grew impatient with his wild living and believe it best to keep a closer eye on him. Liriwen has no intention of returning to those quiet, watchful forests. He has concocted a plan, one sure to prove he is more useful where he is. It would appear the Dwarf Harataki clan has intentions upon Laurelorn territory, something only Liriwen’s quick word could put a stop to._ 

_Of course, this isn’t the case yet, but Dwarfs are so easily led, providing you let them think it’s their idea. Liriwen let slip the location of a stockpile of Dwarf runic artefacts in the Laurelorn, captured during the War of the Beard. Such a treasure could well reverse the exiled Harataki’s fortunes. Liriwen just needs the Characters to get the news to them and make sure the Dwarfs reach the forest’s outskirts, without their growing suspicion. He will take care of the rest._ 

## **Aftermath**
The veracity of the ancient Dwarf artefacts is left deliberately vague. Either Liriwen has leaked a very real stockpile held by the Elves, or he is hoodwinking both Elf and Dwarf. 

Either way, this endeavour has the potential to affect the fortunes of both him and this respected Dwarf clan, in turn upending the entrenched power dynamics of Ubersreik’s Dawihafen. 

Should Liriwen succeed, the prestige he gains in the Laurelorn, and among the Ubersreik underworld as word of his great game gets out, could allow him to become a major player in his own right. No longer dependent upon the Baron or any other such patrons, he becomes the head of his own spy network, and rise from the position of Hireling to become a powerful patron for the Characters. This in turn grants them greater access to both Ubersreik’s criminals and the Laurelorn Forest. 

Meanwhile, the Harataki do not forget this betrayal. The Characters find themselves unwelcome in the company of Dwarfs, while the shame of being manipulated by an Elf leads Queen Vilda to renounce her rank and take the Slayer’s Oath, creating a power vacuum in Dawihafen. 

Failure, on the other hand, sees Liriwen returned to the Laurelorn in shame, and his superiors taking an interest in his associates, who know too much of their methods at this point. Their agents, spread throughout the Old World, keep a close eye upon the Characters, judging whether they are a tool to be used, or a threat to be eliminated.

## **Henrietta ‘Corny’ Cornflower**
## **Halfling Attendant**
## **Motivation:** Ambition
## **Short-Term Ambition:** Raise Her Status.
**Long-term Ambition:** Take her place in the Imperial Court. 

A pretty maidservant in service to one of the Empire’s most respected merchant families, Henrietta Cornflower has her keen eyes set upon the Imperial Court’s heady heights. Her life started humbly enough, working in the fields with the rest of her family, attending the regular parties and feasts that characterise Mootish society and, in general, feeling bored out of her mind. This changed the day a procession of Imperial nobles marched through her village. 

The grand coaches, followed by their supply wagons, were unlike anything Henrietta had ever seen before. While her fathers grumbled about disruption to their harvest, she snuck out to watch as they went by.

To her delight, some nobles stopped to take in the scenery. She marvelled at their colourful clothes, their refined grace, the wonderful food (that mysteriously went missing from their baggage). Nor could she fail to notice the sneer when they spotted her behind the hedgerow. 

Since then, Henrietta has harboured a burning desire to take her rightful place in that world. Against her fathers’ wishes, but with their loving support, she managed to get a place as a kitchen maid for a minor noble. From there, nothing could stop Henrietta’s rise to the middle. She learned that gossip was a currency in her new below-stairs world. Even better, it was currency you could spin from thin air, if you had the right creative flare. She deployed this without mercy, and before long exchanged scrubbing dishes for serving at the table. 

Many years have passed since she first left the Moot, and now Henrietta is personal maidservant to Mistress Ella von Leyen, the matriarch of the wealthy and influential von Leyen trade empire. Here, her ascension has ground to a halt. While at first delighted with the position, Henrietta feels Mistress von Leyen does not approach her noble station with proper decorum. She takes a handson approach to running her trade network, dragging Henrietta all over the Empire, rarely attending balls or galas or any of the other events that, to Henrietta’s mind, are the mark of true nobility. She also insists on calling her by her fathers’ pet name, ‘Corny,’ something that privately infuriates the young Halfling. 

## **Ella Von Leyen**
Loud, brash, and garrulous, Ella von Leyen is an imposing figure. As a young woman, Ella took great pride in personally commanding her family’s ships, captaining trade expeditions as far as the Dwarf hold Karak Kadrin. 

Now in her mid-seventies, Ella may no longer be the one fending off river pirates, but she still makes sure to stay involved in her business. Under her stewardship, the von Leyens have become the main providers of Kadrin Steel in the Empire, prized by Nuln’s Dwarf engineer’s and the various Greatsword companies for their armour. She is rarely found in her family’s Altdorf home, saying she can’t stand any of that gossipy court nonsense, much to the consternation of her long-suffering Halfling maidservant. 

However, age may at last be catching up to her. Those who meet the old woman describe a shadow, her flesh withering away and once-powerful voice cracking at the edges. Her worsening health forces her to rely upon Henrietta, who is more than happy to conduct business on her account. 

Only Henrietta, and perhaps one or two people at the Reform Society, know that this is a weakness of the Halfling’s creation. With a few surreptitious drops of something in the old woman’s tea, Henrietta ensures that her public humiliation is kept to a minimum. She has no intention of killing the woman, but she is sure no one could possibly miss the company of the frightful, old battle axe. 

A recent escape has presented itself to Henrietta in the Reform Society. This social club of young nobles blackballed her mistress after an invitation to discuss trade over drinks resulted in the breaking of a chamber pot over a duke’s head. Yet, in that brief time, the establishment’s owner took an apparent shine to Henrietta, offering her occasional employment whenever she is not needed by her mistress. It is an association Henrietta leapt upon, seeing in the club’s clientele a path to the social acceptance she has always craved. 

## **Corny’s Commands**
## **Quarant-What Now?**
## **Family Matters**
Henrietta’s mistress ordered her to fetch some important goods that just arrived at the docks. Henrietta would not be seen dead in such rough company, and so wonders if the Characters might assist in this little matter. They needn’t worry about the ship being quarantined for disease; she is sure it is just something the harbourmaster is saying to keep the riff raff away. 

Henrietta’s fathers are in town. Oh gods, what if anyone were to find them and discover she is not actually from Mootish gentry? She cannot risk the humiliation. Could the Characters keep them busy and safe for the day? Maybe take them around the market, show them a few taverns, but keep an eye out. You never know who might jump on an opening like this. And for goodness’ sake, stop them from asking everyone if they know where their ‘dear little Corny’ is! 

## **Just a Spoonful**
Henrietta’s stores of her mistress’s medicine are starting to grow thin. A courier should have arrived with the latest batch, but while his boat has docked, the courier was not on it. Nor can anyone on board remember seeing him leave. The last thing anyone recalls, he was standing on the dock when they stopped to take on supplies, looking out at the river with an odd, dreamlike expression in his eyes. 

## **You Shall Go to the Ball**
A duke extended an invitation to Henrietta’s mistress, but to her horror the old baggage turned him down! Henrietta simply must attend, there are some people there from a local social club who said they would be quite interested in talking to her. If she were to adjust her mistress’s invitation, and the Characters posed as her entourage, she is sure they would be able to present themselves as true nobility. 

## **Keep a Good Man Down**
Henrietta has a friend who needs discreet assistance — she is sure the Characters would be more than capable of removing a dead body from a local dinner party with all due discretion. Now, how do they feel about one that refuses to stay dead? Quietly, mind! She wouldn’t want to disrupt the guests, who are having such a lovely get-together. 

## **The Grey Lady Reform Society**
The Grey Lady Reform Society is a social club for Imperial gentility. Anyone with important connections in the Vobergland, provided they are vouched for by two members, can come to drink, dine, and discuss the need for change as the noble families stave off the merchants’ and wizards’ growing influence. 

The club is owned by Rupert Lehman, a slight, balding man of impeccable manners. He is rarely seen outside of his various clubs, watching over its clientele and selecting from among them those to invite into the exclusive ‘Back Rooms’. 

Few realise this shadow of a man is a scion of the infamous von Carstein vampiric bloodline, working to prepare the way for his masters’ coming. He recently fixed his eyes upon the von Leyens and their trade connections with the Dwarfs. An interruption here could prove costly indeed for the Empire’s armies, and while his first attempt to draw them in did not go as he had hoped, Henrietta represents a new path to pursue. 

## **For Hire: Life Below Stairs**
Henrietta will not deign to work for someone of Brass Status. She will, however, employ their services, making her a potential Patron for low-Status parties. 

Henrietta can be hired for etiquette training, assisting in the **Reputation** Endeavour. Doing so reduces the cost of the Endeavour to half the Character’s maximum Earning income and changes the Career Skill Test from **Challenging (+0)** to **Easy (+10)** . Scoring an Astounding Failure, however, makes Henrietta try to distance herself from the Character. 

She can also accompany Characters, helping maintain a ruse of wealth or granting them access to places beyond their usual station, thanks to her connections with other servants. 

Henrietta costs 3/– for a Quick Job, 9/– Daily, and 3 GC 4/– Weekly. 

A Character of Gold Status can take Henrietta as a Henchman (WFRP, page 309), giving permanent access to her assistance while costing half the Character’s Earning income to maintain her employment. 

## **Prestige Adventure Beyond Reproach**
_Rupert Lehman, organiser of the Reform Society, came to Henrietta with a proposition. The merchant families are eroding the power and respectability of the nobility, but he sees in Henrietta someone in whom the old standards might be upheld. He has come up with a plan to grant her control of the von Leyen trade empire. All she needs is to get her mistress’s signature on some specific paperwork, which Henrietta knows is kept secured at her lawyers’ offices in Altdorf, and then arrange for her subsequent passing. No possible suspicion can fall on Henrietta for this to work, so she must ask the Characters for their assistance._ 

_However, Ella von Leyen has cottoned on to Corny’s little games. She has been pretending to be an invalid, while carrying out her own investigations into the Reform Society’s darker side. The Characters could be useful allies in uncovering the truth._ 

## **Henrietta’s Medicine**
Distilled from Heartkill (WFRP, page 306), this poison is diluted to provide only 2 poison conditions. Normally, it would be far too expensive for a servant to afford. 

## **Aftermath**
Should the Characters succeed in elevating Henrietta, she sees they are richly rewarded — for the time being. They gain access to the Von Leyen shipping network, with free passage wherever they choose, and the offer to act as Henrietta’s representatives to Karak Kadrin. Of course, the Characters are loose ends in Henrietta’s schemes and need to be disposed of. It would be such a tragedy if their ship were to sink one day. 

Rupert Lehman considers Henrietta’s agents a potential future asset. Perhaps they might like to take their place in the Reform Society and mix with the Empire’s upper classes. Should they prove themselves worthy, one day they may be invited into the coveted Back Rooms, where Lehman introduces his chosen to the new order that is to come. 

If the Characters assist Ella von Leyen in uncovering the Reform Society’s vampiric nature, Imperial nobility is plunged into upheaval. Anyone connected to the Society comes under the scrutiny of the Witch Hunters and the Black Guards of Morr, leaving many bastions of Imperial power at their political rivals’ mercy. The Characters are caught in a shadow war between nobles, religious cults, and vampires, and need to choose their side carefully. 

## **Angela the Red**
## **Human Hunter**
## **Motive:** Loyalty
**Short-term Ambition:** Protect the Taalhoffer lands. **Long-term Ambition:** End the unholy hunt. 

A quiet woman of short, powerful stature, Angela the Red is an intense person to be around, but few question her skill with horse, hound, and hawk. She serves as the Master of the Hunt for Lord Hans Taalhoffer and gained her nickname from the way she comes to life when the hunt begins. Her dour demeanour is taken over by fierce joy and, some whisper, her eyes begin to flash a brilliant crimson. 

Angela has always had a way with animals. As a young girl working in the Lord Taalhoffer’s stables, she gained favour for how quickly the horses came to trust her. People marvelled to find wild birds of prey settling in branches near her, or spied Angela holding a skittish wolf ’s gaze. 

## **Angela the Red Human Huntsmaster (Silver 3)**

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | 32 | 43 | 26 | 42 | 26 | 27 | 35 | 28 | 33 | 35 | 13 |

**Traits:** Mutation (Crimson Eyes), Ranged (Bow) +5 (60), Weapon (Knife) +3 

**Skills:** Animal Care 48, Charm Animal 48, Climb 31, Cool 38, Endurance 47, Haggle 38, Melee (Basic 35), Lore (Reikland 33, Beasts 42), Language (Magick) 30, Outdoor Perception 31, Ranged (Bow 53), Set Trap 40, Stealth (Rural) 32, Survival 31 

**Talents:** Acute Sense (Sight), Deadeye Shot, Fearless (Animals), Hunter’s Eye, Marksman, Robust, Rover, Strider (Woodland), Trapper, Witch! 

**Spells:** Animal Friend 

**Trappings:** Bow and 20 arrows, Dog Whistle, Fur cloak, Taalhoffer seal, Tinderbox 

Such a reputation can be dangerous. It is only by Lord Taalhoffer’s swift intervention that Angela escaped a Witch Hunter’s tender mercies. 

Angela believes herself blessed by Taal, gifted with words to make any creature listen. Even so, she worries about the sheer thrill she finds hunting, the way it makes her blood sing and the triumph when she catches her mark. She watches herself constantly for any sign the Witch Hunter’s suspicions could be true, and her gifts mark her as one of the damned. This constant vigil has taken a toll on Angela, leaving her restrained and cold to her fellows. 

Angela does have one close friend. Helena Taalhoffer, her lord’s daughter and heir, takes the same, fierce joy in the hunt Angela does. Angela delighted in teaching Helena all about tracking, horse riding, and the ways to make hawk and hound respond to your command, finding in her an eager pupil. However, in recent days she has noticed an unsettling change come over Helena. 

Helena is taking less satisfaction in the pursuit of a clean hunt, revelling instead in slaughter. More than once, Angela has had to take the killing blow, putting a poor creature out of its misery after Helena’s careful aim left it bleeding its last from a dozen painful wounds. Worse still are the rumours. In the taverns, peasants tell stories about midnight hunts, of wild screams, and raucous laughter in the night. Of people never making it home. 

Now, Angela spends her evenings away from Taalhoffer Keep as much as possible. She drinks alone, listening for gossip and wrestling with her conscience. She owes the Taalhoffers much and is loath to bring suspicion to their door. But she knows that this cannot last. And always, lurking at the edges of her mind, there is the fear that she too might one day give in to the voices urging her to the hunt. 

## **The Taalhoffers**
## **Lord Hans Taalhoffer**
Lord Hans Taalhoffer was a great warrior, once. In his youth, he gained renown serving alongside the former Emperor, earning the right to stand amidst his Reiksguard. Now, those days are long behind him. While on the battlefield, he found himself overcome by bloodlust. He emerged from the red mist a scared and broken man, surrounded by slaughtered enemies, and praise from allies who had not been close enough to see his frenzy. 

These days, Hans is devoted to the service of Taal, his family’s patron. The only time he leaves his keep is to establish some new shrine or altar to the god of the wilds. The rest of the time, he stays in his study, working on a manuscript detailing the finer points of fencing etiquette. 

As a young man, Hans was something of a philanderer. The result was Angela. The appearance of an illegitimate first child caused his wife a great deal of pain. While he cares for the girl, Hans has ensured that no one, save his daughter Helena, know of Angela’s true lineage. 

## **Helena Taalhoffer**
Helena Taalhoffer is her father’s youth returned. While she sees no need to go searching for glory in battle, she is skilled with both bow and boar spear, showing that same vibrant life that characterised the Lord Taalhoffer’s younger days. 

As a girl, she heard a voice whispering to her from the woods. It encouraged her to hunt, telling her the best places to find prey. At first, she believed it to be Taal, and gave herself over to the voice’s urgings. Now, she is not sure who it is. Nor does she care. The Whisperer has opened her mind to the hunt’s true joys and her blood sings with each kill she delivers to its altar, hidden in an overgrown grove where the light never quite reaches. 

She started to bring others into her hunting troupe, fellow young nobles looking for their chance to prove themselves to the Whisperer. Together, they have taken to pursuing a far more challenging prey: Humans. After all, the forests are dangerous, and no one will question the disappearance of a few peasants. 

Helena hopes, one day, to bring Angela into the fold. She sees the chains of fear the hunter wraps around herself and knows that she too hears the whispers. She must be cautious. Angela is devoted to Taal, and to her father. But a hunter learns patience.

## **The Whisperer in the Woods**
This entity is left deliberately vague. Perhaps they are an imprisoned Daemon of Chaos, or the spirit of Morghur, the eternal avatar of corruption. They could even be a god from the time before the Empire, such as Ahalt the Drinker, eager to reclaim the land that was theirs. 

## **Angela’s Appeals in Sheep’s Clothing**
There are reports of a creature attacking local livestock, making away with their skins and leaving the bloody carcasses behind. Some blame wolves, others say it’s Orcs, while in the taverns people mutter of things darker still. Whatever it is, Angela has been tasked with hunting it down, and she needs the Characters to act as beaters to drive the creature out of the undergrowth and towards her. 

## **Fall Far from the Tree**
The trees in Lord Taalhoffer’s orchards are showing signs of disease. A rotten stench hangs thick in the air and their bark peels away in bloody tatters. Despite this, the fruit is perfect, rich, red and inviting. Angela heard that a roving band of Wood Elves are camped nearby. Perhaps they might know how to cure these trees, before someone gives into temptation and takes a bite for themselves. 

## **Who Hunts the Hunter?**
A travelling Witch Hunter has gone missing, their gear found lying at the side of a road in the woods nearby. Angela must prove this couldn’t be the work of Humans, or else more of the stern killers are sure to turn up. The witch hunter was last seen sleeping in the stables of a nearby tavern, a place with an ill reputation as a favoured drinking den for local highwaymen. But surely even they would think twice before risking Sigmar’s wrath. 

## **Call of the Wild**
Lord Taalhoffer’s prized hound escaped, savaging one of its handlers in the process. Angela always found it a rather placid creature but noticed a change after Helena ordered it be given new food. She needs to get to the bottom of this, before any other hounds go feral. Meanwhile, stories come in from the surrounding hamlets of a giant, wolf-like monster, with glowing, emerald eyes. 

## **Old War Stories**
The Taalhoffer’s dungeons are occupied for the first time in Angela’s memory. An old vagrant came through town, begging for coins and talking about how she once served in the military alongside Lord Taalhoffer. Apparently, she has a few tales she is sure everyone would love to hear. Lord Taalhoffer disagreed. What could be so dangerous about a vagrant’s rambling anecdotes? Angela wants to hear these stories but can’t risk being found breaking into the Taalhoffer dungeons herself. 

## **For Hire: Walk in My Footsteps**
Angela can be hired by any Character to train them in **Tracking** (WFRP, page 131) or **Ride (Horse)** (WFRP, page 129). Alternatively, the Characters can hire her as a local scout and tracker to aid them during an adventure, but only in forests and countryside. She is not comfortable in cities, preferring to stay away from crowds, but if circumstances force her, all Track Tests she makes in such places will be **Difficult (−10)** . 

Angela does not care for coin, and can only be hired on a favour-for-a-favour basis. However, she does accept payment as per the **Training** rules (WFRP, page 199) for the purpose of this Endeavour. 

## **Prestige Adventure Red in Tooth and Claw**
_Three savaged Human corpses were left scattered upon an altar to Taal. Locals are whispering about monsters, but Angela knows it is far worse, and she can no longer turn a blind eye. She needs the Characters’ help to set a trap for these hunters, and to do that they need to find out when and where they will next play their little games. If they are careful, they could make the trap look like an accident and avoid further shame falling on the Taalhoffers._ 

Helping Angela stop Helena places her in the Characters’ debt. She offers them her services whenever needed, potentially accompanying the party as a Henchman. However, the loss of his daughter sends Lord Taalhoffer into despair. His ordered life slips away, giving into the bloodlust. The first sign is his work on fencing etiquette changing to a heretical text. Influenced by the Whisperer, Taalhoffer spreads knowledge of the altars throughout the Empire’s aristocracy. After a while, he will begin the hunts again, forcing Angela to call on the Characters for assistance. Together, perhaps they can find a way to end this evil. 

_Helena Taalhoffer, however, has her own plans. Angela is to be the next mark for their hunt. If she can drive her and the Characters to her patron’s altar, she is sure they will join her bloody entourage. All they must do is make a choice: offer a sacrifice or become the sacrifice._ 

## **Aftermath**
Should anyone be killed near the altar, their blood weakens whatever bindings hold the entity. Its presence starts drawing vicious predators to the woods, which could mean more mercenary work in the short term. Sooner or later though, the monsters become too many. 

Anyone who chooses to make the sacrifice will automatically gain the _Unholy Rage_ mental corruption (WFRP, page 185). Their sleep becomes haunted by strange dreams, showing other altars scattered throughout the Old World.
